title: Borcea-Branden AIM problems
certificate_tex: Stable degree-five polynomial plus size-five immanant POT obstruction.

provenance.statement_tex:
Characterize all symmetric, real stable and homogeneous polynomial of degree $d$ in $n$ variables.  Is it in fact so that if $p$ is such a polynomial, then there is a $d\times d$ positive semidefinite $d\times d$ matrix $A$ such that
\[p(z_1,\ldots,z_n)=\eta(z_1A,\ldots,z_nA)?\]
This is not obvious even for $n=2$.

title: Borcea-Branden AIM problems
certificate_tex: Exact Schur expansion; four violating partitions.

provenance.statement_tex:
Lieb's Permanent-On-Top (POT) Conjecture for the symmetric group on $d$ elements [J,L] asserts that if $A$ is a $d\times d$ positive semi-definite matrix then $\Imm_\lambda(A)\le f^\lambda\per(A)$ for all $\lambda\vdash d$.  An affirmative answer to the following problem would in particular imply the validity of the POT Conjecture.

\emph{Problem 38.}  Let $p$ be as in Problem 36.  Is $a_\lambda\le f^\lambda a_{(1^d)}$ for all $\lambda\vdash d$?

title: Borcea-Branden AIM problems
certificate_tex: Positive-definite $5\times5$ det-pencil; exact Schur expansion with $[s_{(1^5)}]q=-2972$.

provenance.statement_tex:
Let $p$ be a symmetric, real stable and homogeneous polynomial of degree $d$ in $n$ variables with $d\le n$ and suppose that $p$ has at least one positive (and then all non-negative) coefficients in the monomial basis.  Is $p$ Schur-positive?  That is, when $p(z_1,\ldots,z_n)$ is expanded in the Schur-basis
\[p(z_1,\ldots,z_n)=\sum_{\lambda\vdash d}a_\lambda s_\lambda(z_1,\ldots,z_n),\]
is $a_\lambda\ge0$ for all $\lambda\vdash d$?

title: Borcea-Branden AIM problems
certificate_tex: Schur-positive member of the same family; $a_{(1^5)}=69<125=f^{(1^5)}a_{(5)}$.

provenance.statement_tex:
If $A$ is a $d\times d$ matrix then $\det(A)=\Imm_{(1^d)}(A)$ and $\per(A)=\Imm_{(d)}(A)$, where $(1^d)=(1,\ldots,1)$ and $(d)=(1^d)'=(d,0,\ldots,0)$.  Schur's inequality [J,L] asserts that if $A$ is a $d\times d$ positive semi-definite matrix then $\Imm_\lambda(A)\ge f^\lambda\det(A)$ for all $\lambda\vdash d$, where $f^\lambda$ is the number of standard Young tableaux of shape $\lambda$.  A natural real stable extension of this result would be as follows.

\emph{Problem 37.}  Let $p$ be as in Problem 36.  Is $a_\lambda\ge f^\lambda a_{(d)}$ for all $\lambda\vdash d$?

title: Macdonald lattice Schur-convexity
certificate_tex: Rank-two Schur specialization, valid for every $0<r<1$.

provenance.statement_tex:
For all $q,t\in(0,1)$, $a>0$, and $x\in\mathcal L_n^{q,t,a}$, the function $\lambda\mapsto\Omega_\lambda(x;q,t)$ is log-convex and Schur-convex.

Here, by \S2.1 of the same paper, $\Omega_\lambda(x;q,t)=P_\lambda(x;q,t)/P_\lambda(t^\delta;q,t)$ is the Macdonald polynomial normalized to $1$ at the principal specialization $t^\delta=(t^{n-1},t^{n-2},\ldots,1)$, and the scaled, $t$-shifted, dominant $q$-lattice is
\[\mathcal L_n=\mathcal L_n^{q,t,a}=\left\{(aq^{-\mu_1}t^{n-1},aq^{-\mu_2}t^{n-2},\ldots,aq^{-\mu_n}):(\mu_1\ge\ldots\ge\mu_n)\in\mathbb Z^n\right\}\subset\R^n.\]

provenance.source_tex: G.~Csordas \citeyearpar{Csordas2014}, Open Problem 4.13, restating Coffey--Csordas Conjecture 2.5
provenance.statement_tex:
([5, Conjecture 2.5])  Show that the derivatives of the Jacobi theta function, $\Phi(t)$, are (strictly) log-concave on $\R$; that is, for each $n\in\mathbb N$,
\[J_n(t):=(\Phi^{(n)}(t))^2-\Phi^{(n-1)}(t)\Phi^{(n+1)}(t)>0\quad\text{for }t\in\R.\]
Here, by (4.2) of the same paper, the Jacobi theta function (without the usual factor $4$) is $\Phi(t):=\sum_{n\ge1}\pi n^2\left(2\pi n^2e^{4t}-3\right)\exp\left(5t-\pi n^2e^{4t}\right)$.

title: Variance-sensitive Matrix Spencer
certificate_tex: Exact $d=n$ diagonal family: $\disc=(m-1)/\sqrt m$ against variance $1+1/m$, a ratio of $\Theta(\sqrt{\log n})$.

provenance.statement_tex:
There exists a universal constant $C$, such that for any choice of $n$ symmetric matrices $A_1,\ldots,A_n\in\R^{n\times n}$ satisfying $\|A_i\|_{\rm op}\le1$ there exists a coloring $x\in\{\pm1\}^n$, such that
\[\left\|\sum_{i=1}^nx_iA_i\right\|_{\rm op}\le C\left\|\sum_{i=1}^nA_i^2\right\|_{\rm op}^{1/2}.\]

title: A mixed-norm Cauchy-Schwarz question of Sah, Sawhney, Stoner and Zhao
certificate_tex: Nonnegative integer $A,B\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{3\times2}$ at $p=q=3/2$; the deficit is an integer combination of integer square roots, negative by exact algebraic evaluation.

provenance.source_tex: A.~Sah, M.~Sawhney, D.~Stoner and Y.~Zhao, the open question stated immediately after inequality~(3.1) in \S3

title: Quantum coupon collection: positivity of an alternating sum of inverses
certificate_tex: Exact rational $3\times3$ matrices with $n=6$ and the integer vector $(4,1,3)^{\mathsf T}$ give a quadratic form strictly between $-96$ and $-95$.

provenance.statement_tex:
Here we take symmetric positive definite matrices $X_1,\ldots,X_n\in\mathbf{S}_{++}^d$, and consider the sum
\[
Q_n(X_1,\ldots,X_n):=\sum_{k=1}^n(-1)^{k+1}
\sum_{1\le i_1<\cdots<i_k\le n}\left(X_{i_1}+\cdots+X_{i_k}\right)^{-1}.
\]

\textbf{Conjecture.} For $n\ge1$, and $X_1,\ldots,X_n\in\mathbf{S}_{++}^d$, we have $Q_n(X_1,\ldots,X_n)\succ0$.

\emph{Note.} The cases $n=1,2,3$ are trivially true.  I've tried $n=4$ numerically, and it seems to hold.  (Also, by CCP, positivity immediately holds for simultaneously diagonalizable matrices.)

title: No dimension-free constant in O'Donnell's matrix conjecture
certificate_tex: An exact algebraic Givens-rotation family with a rational dyadic lower bound, accompanied by a standard-library exact-arithmetic verifier.

provenance.source_tex:
R.~O'Donnell, answering a question of Nengkun Yu on MathOverflow
\cite{ODonnell2015AlmostDiagonal}, reports that he and J.~Wright had been
considering the problem in connection with quantum tomography, and closes by
conjecturing the unit-trace case.  The same conjecture was put to S.~Sra by
O'Donnell in personal communication.
provenance.statement_tex:
The question answered was whether a positive semidefinite $M$ with
$\lVert D(M)-\Lambda(M)\rVert_1\leq\epsilon$ must lie within $2\epsilon$ of
conjectures the normalized case:

\begin{quote}
``If you restrict $M$ to have trace $1$, then we felt the desired result was
true but with a weaker conclusion of $O(\sqrt\epsilon)$ rather than
$2\epsilon$.''
\end{quote}

Written out, and with the implied constant absolute: for every unit-trace
positive semidefinite $R$ with eigenvalues $\lambda_i$ and diagonal entries
$d_{ii}$,
\[
  \lVert R-\operatorname{Diag}(R)\rVert_1^2
  \leq c\nlsum_i |\lambda_i-d_{ii}|
\]
for some absolute constant $c$ independent of $n$.

title: Feasible Picard steps for DPP likelihood
certificate_tex: Exact rational $2\times2$ feasible update with lower likelihood.

provenance.statement_tex:
Above we showed that for $a=1$ ascent is guaranteed.  Empirically, $a>1$ often works well; Prop.~A.1 presents an easily computable upper bound on feasible $a$.  We conjecture that for all feasible values $a\ge1$, iteration (2.5) is guaranteed to increase the log-likelihood.

The iteration carrying the step size is $L_{k+1}=L_k+aL_k\Delta_kL_k$, displayed as (2.7) in the source; feasibility is the bound $a\le1/(1-\gamma)$ of Prop.~A.1.

title: Log-volume midpoint gap and its Lorentzian generalization
certificate_tex: Strictly Lorentzian rational cubic realized as a Steiner polynomial in $\R^3$; exact rational triangle-violation bound $>7.15\times10^{-3}$.

provenance.source_tex: S.~Sra, standalone problem posed in 2012; formulation as recorded in the audit of Appendix~\ref{sec:lorentzianaudit}
provenance.statement_tex:
The log-volume midpoint gap is the square of a distance on convex bodies: that is,
\[d_{\Vol}(K,L):=\left[\log\Vol\!\left(\frac{K+L}{2}\right)-\tfrac12\log\Vol(K)-\tfrac12\log\Vol(L)\right]^{1/2}\]
is a semimetric on convex bodies.

title: Log-volume midpoint gap and its Lorentzian generalization

certificate_tex: The same cubic read as a homogeneous Lorentzian polynomial; the violation transfers verbatim.

provenance.source_tex: S.~Sra, standalone problem posed in 2019 as a Lorentzian generalization of the log-volume statement; formulation as recorded in the audit of Appendix~\ref{sec:lorentzianaudit}
provenance.statement_tex:
Let $\mathcal C\subset\R^m$ be an open convex cone, let $G:\mathcal C\to(0,\infty)$, and put $F=-\log G$ and
\[\J_G(x,y):=\frac{F(x)+F(y)}2-F\!\left(\frac{x+y}{2}\right).\]
If $G$ is homogeneous and Lorentzian, then $d_G:=\sqrt{\J_G}$ is a semimetric.

title: An oblivious subspace injection need not give relative-error sketch-and-solve
certificate_tex:
Three exact rationally weighted $2\times2$ sketch atoms, with exact isotropy,
an exact $99/100$ injection guarantee, and exact squared residual ratios.

provenance.source_tex:
Problem~5.1 of the Simons workshop report of Amsel et al.
\cite{AmselEtAl2026}, scribed for Section~5 by Raphael A. Meyer.  Townsend and
Wang \cite{TownsendWang2026} had already resolved the general question; this
witness is independent and claims no priority.
provenance.statement_tex:
Let $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}$ be a full-rank matrix,
$B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}$ be a matrix, and let
$\Omega\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times k}$ be an oblivious subspace injection with
dimension $d$ and injectivity $1-\varepsilon$. Let
$\widetilde{X}=(\Omega^{\top}A)^{+}(\Omega^{\top}B)\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times p}$
be the sketch-and-solve approximation to the ordinary least-squares solution
$X=A^{+}B$. (Here, ${}^{+}$ denotes the Moore--Penrose pseudoinverse.) Prove
or disprove: Does it necessarily hold that
\[
\|A\widetilde{X}-B\|_{\rm F}\leq(1+\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon))
\min_{X\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times p}}\|AX-B\|_{\rm F}?
\]

title: Exact QRCP can miss the orthonormal-row conditioning bound
